· success, exit status, signal, timeout, spawn failure and handoff
  ▎$ run     go test ./...                                 ok · 1 line   1.2s
  ▎✗ run     go test ./...                                      exit 1   2.0s
    stderr: test failed
  ▎✗ run     build                                   killed · signal 9   3.0s
    compiler stopped
  ▎✗ run     go test ./...                              timed out · 1s   1.0s
    partial output
  ▎✗ run     missing containment binary                  did not start      —
    fork/exec bwrap: no such file
  ▎$ run     watch                                         ok · 1 line   1.0s


· did not start · working-directory
  ▎✗ run     go test ./...                 did not start · working dir      —
    working directory unavailable: /work/.claude/worktrees/gone — chdir
    /bin/bash: no such file or directory
    Nothing ran: a command's working directory has to be there when it
    starts. Find out where it went — a worktree or checkout removed under a
    running session is the usual cause — and run the command somewhere that
    still exists.


· did not start · execution-shell
  ▎✗ run     go test ./...             did not start · execution shell      —
    execution shell unavailable: fork/exec /usr/local/bin/bash: no such file
    or directory
    Nothing ran, and nothing will until that shell is back: every command
    here goes through it, so another spelling of the same command reaches the
    same missing program. Report it.


· did not start · containment
  ▎✗ run     go test ./...                 did not start · containment      —
    containment unavailable: fork/exec /usr/bin/bwrap: no such file or
    directory
    Nothing ran, and it was not run uncontained — that is the one
    substitution this session will not make. Report the mechanism as missing;
    `shhh doctor` says what this host needs.


· did not start · permission
  ▎✗ run     ./deploy.sh                    did not start · permission      —
    permission denied: fork/exec ./deploy.sh: permission denied
    Nothing ran. The refusal is the operating system's and not a decision
    this session made or can undo, so use a program and a path the current
    user is already allowed, or report what is refusing it.


· did not start · spawn
  ▎✗ run     go test ./...                       did not start · spawn      —
    spawn refused: fork/exec /bin/bash: resource temporarily unavailable
    Nothing ran, and the reason above is the host's rather than the
    command's. Retry only if that reason names something that has since
    changed; otherwise report it.


· ran, and nobody could read how it ended
  ▎✗ run     make release                             did not complete   4.0s
    packaging…
    wait: read |0: file already closed
